title: SAEs on a grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer: against a provable Fourier ground truth the raw neuron basis is 0.75 frequency-pure and the best usable SAE only 0.32 - the sparsity prior fights the density of the true features
hypothesis: A small overcomplete L1 sparse autoencoder trained on the MLP hidden activations of a fully grokked (a+b) mod 59 transformer will recover the model's known Fourier structure: a large fraction of its alive features will be frequency-pure (>=80% of their 2D Fourier power on a single frequency k) and the set of frequencies claimed by those features will match the model's key frequencies.
question: In the one interpretability setting with a PROVABLE answer key - a grokked modular-addition transformer, which is known to implement Fourier multiplication - do SAE features actually recover the ground-truth Fourier units, are all key frequencies recovered, and how does SAE faithfulness compare against the standard-basis (raw neuron) baseline that everyone skips?
method: No training of the task model: the fully grokked checkpoint (train acc 1.000, test acc 1.000, verified in-run at 1.0000 accuracy on all 3481 pairs) is LOADED from the sibling run 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition/model.pt, together with its saved key_freqs [24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25]. Activation site: post-ReLU MLP hidden layer (d_mlp = 256) evaluated on ALL p^2 = 3481 inputs; activations are norm-scaled so E||x|| = sqrt(d) which makes the L1 coefficient comparable across models. SAE: standard ReLU dictionary (f = ReLU((x - b_dec) W_enc + b_enc), x_hat = f W_dec + b_dec), decoder rows renormalised to unit norm every step, L1 penalty on f, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 256, 2500 steps, dead-feature resampling at 40% and 70% of training. Arms: 4x expansion (1024 features) at three sparsity coefficients lambda in {0.3, 1.0, 3.0} on each of three activation sources, plus one extra 8x (2048-feature) grokked arm at lambda = 1.0 = 10 SAEs. GROUND-TRUTH SCORE: build the orthonormal real 2D Fourier basis over (a,b) in Z_59 x Z_59; frequency k's block is the 3x3 span {1, cos w_k a, sin w_k a} x {1, cos w_k b, sin w_k b} minus DC, and these blocks are disjoint once DC is dropped, so purity = max_k power_k / (total non-DC power) is a genuine partition statistic. A unit is PURE iff purity >= 0.8 and ALIVE iff it fires on >= 1% of the 3481 inputs. Two purity views per feature: (i) activation-map purity, the spectrum of the feature's own firing pattern f(a,b); (ii) decoder-direction purity, the spectrum of w_f . x(a,b) read out by the feature's unit-norm decoder direction - view (ii) ignores the ReLU gate and is deliberately the metric most favourable to the SAE. For a raw neuron the two coincide. FOUR CONTROLS: (1) the raw 256 MLP neurons scored with the identical metric (the head-to-head baseline); (2) SAEs on model_mid.pt, the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint (test acc 0.102); (3) SAEs on a random-init transformer of the same architecture; (4) random-unit-direction and random-sparse-indicator-map nulls for the purity statistic itself. An arm is flagged COLLAPSED (and excluded from the headline, but still reported) if FVU > 0.25 or fewer than 10 features are alive, so that a dead autoencoder cannot claim a trivially perfect purity.
architecture: frozen 1-layer attention+MLP transformer, no LayerNorm, no biases, d_model 64 / 4 heads / d_mlp 256 / vocab 60, 56,960 params (loaded, not trained) + 10 ReLU sparse autoencoders, 4x (1024 feat, 0.53M params) and 8x (2048 feat, 1.05M params) over the 256-dim MLP hidden layer

dataset.name: MLP hidden activations of a grokked transformer on all 59^2 = 3481 (a,b) pairs of (a+b) mod 59; same for a memorized checkpoint and a random-init model
dataset.source: checkpoints from experiments/2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition (model.pt, model_mid.pt); inputs generated in run.py

task: sparse-dictionary recovery of a known ground-truth feature basis (Fourier features of a grokked modular-addition circuit)
compute: CPU single-threaded, 486.8s total (10 SAEs, 38-88s each) against a 640s training budget; no arm was skipped

metrics.reproducibility: two back-to-back runs produced identical results.json apart from per-arm wall-clock fields

result_summary: The hypothesis is REFUTED, and the sharpest number is the baseline nobody runs. Against a provable answer key, the RAW MLP NEURON BASIS of the grokked model is already 0.750 frequency-pure (mean purity 0.827, median 0.9257, 192 of 256 neurons pure) while the best NON-COLLAPSED SAE reaches only 0.318 (8x expansion, lambda=1.0) and the best 4x arm only 0.105. Even the deliberately SAE-friendly decoder-direction metric, which ignores the ReLU gate, peaks at 0.568 - still below the neurons. The SAE does not beat doing nothing. (2) SPARSITY IS THE CAUSE, AND THE PURE LIMIT IS DEGENERATE: purity rises monotonically with the L1 coefficient (0.120 -> 0.334 -> 0.917 mean) but so does FVU (0.009 -> 0.068 -> 0.990). The only arm that is 100% pure explains 1% of the variance with ONE surviving feature out of 1024 - a collapsed autoencoder, not an interpretation. Every arm that actually reconstructs is <= 0.32 pure. The mechanism is structural rather than a tuning failure: a true Fourier feature cos(w_k(a+b)) is DENSE (nonzero almost everywhere on the grid) while L1 rewards features that fire rarely - alive SAE features fire on 6.6-21.7% of inputs against 62.6% for the average neuron, and a localised indicator is spectrally broad by construction. The sparsity prior and the ground-truth feature shape are in direct conflict. (3) NO ARM RECOVERS THE KEY-FREQUENCY SET - BUT NEITHER DO THE NEURONS, AND THAT IS ITSELF A FINDING: the checkpoint's saved key_freqs (top-6 of the EMBEDDING spectrum) are {24, 17, 5, 3, 6, 25}, but the MLP layer only uses FOUR - all 192 pure neurons claim {3, 5, 17, 24}, holding 97.0% of neuron activation power, while freq 25 holds 0.65% and freq 6 holds 0.32%, less than frequency 11 which is not a key freq at all. So the embedding-derived key-frequency set OVER-COUNTS the algorithm the MLP actually runs by two, and any 'did the SAE find all key freqs' test inherits that. The best SAE arm claims a strict SUBSET, {5, 17, 24}, dropping frequency 3 entirely, with 0.911 of its dictionary dead. (4) CONTROLS ALL LAND WHERE THEY SHOULD: SAEs on the memorized-not-generalizing checkpoint are 0.000 pure at every lambda (max mean purity 0.092) and SAEs on a random-init transformer are 0.000 pure; raw neurons of those two models score 0.137 and 0.131 mean purity; random sparse indicator maps score 0.005. The metric is not 'any SAE looks pure' - the grokked model is the only source with recoverable structure and the SAE partially finds it. (5) A CAVEAT THAT CUTS AGAINST OUR OWN SAE-FRIENDLY METRIC: a RANDOM unit direction in the grokked activation space already scores 0.482 mean purity (p99 = 0.80), because that space is spanned by only 4 frequencies, so decoder-direction purity has a high null and the 0.638 mean at lambda=1.0 is a real but modest lift. The activation-map metric has a near-zero null (0.005) and is the honest one - and it is the metric on which the SAE does worst. CAVEATS, worst first: ONE SEED, one model, one site (MLP hidden; the post-attention residual stream was not swept, for budget); only 3 sparsity coefficients and 2 expansions; 2500 SAE steps on a fully-enumerated 3481-point dataset the SAE could in principle memorize; only the plain L1/ReLU SAE was tested, so this says nothing about top-k, JumpReLU or matryoshka variants that decouple L0 from per-feature density - which is exactly the mitigation the density mechanism predicts and the obvious next run; model_mid.pt comes from a different train/test split than model.pt (inherited from the sibling experiment), which does not affect its use here since activations are taken on all p^2 inputs; and the COLLAPSED-arm rule (FVU <= 0.25 and >= 10 alive) is a judgement call, fixed before purity was inspected.

novelty_check.conclusion: Partial prior art on every ingredient, none on the combination. The general claim that SAEs recover plausible-but-non-canonical units is the ICLR 2025 canonical-units critique (openreview HpUs2EXjOl, 'Rethinking Evaluation of Sparse Autoencoders'), listed in the backlog; the Fourier answer key and the frequency-purity style of neuron scoring are Nanda et al. 2301.05217; arXiv:2402.16726 analyses circuits in grokked transformers on modular polynomials but not with SAEs; the SAE recipe is Bricken et al. 'Towards Monosemanticity' / ARENA 3.1; and openreview DSOTgzeH3w ('On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders: A Theoretical Framework and Reweighted Remedy') gives theory that L1 SAEs are biased against high-density features, which is precisely the mechanism isolated empirically here. To our search, no prior work scores SAE features against the PROVABLE Fourier answer key of a grokked modular-addition transformer with (i) the raw neuron basis as a head-to-head baseline, (ii) memorized and random-init models as negative controls, and (iii) a random-direction null for the purity statistic itself. The three additions are the contribution - in particular the finding that the standard basis BEATS the learned dictionary (0.75 vs 0.32) and that the gap is explained by feature density rather than SAE tuning. The grokked model and the purity metric are replications. Search was web-only (arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this box); the two 2026-dated hits that surfaced were not leaned on for numbers.

title: The merge breakpoint: correlated feature pairs never choose local orthogonality - unequal importance kills the weak member by amplitude decay along the SAME direction, and anticorrelated values only bend the merge to |cos| 0.64-0.75
hypothesis: The pair-merging seen at equal importance in 2026-07-23_superposition-correlation-phase breaks down under two stressors - unequal within-pair importance, and anticorrelated within-pair VALUES - and past some breakpoint the pair abandons its shared direction for a locally orthogonal basis (within-pair |cos| < 0.7).
question: When does pair-merging in the Anthropic toy model become too lossy? Where is the breakpoint in within-pair importance ratio r, or in within-pair value correlation c, at which the merged pair splits into a locally orthogonal basis?
method: Anthropic-style toy autoencoder ReLU(W^T W x + b), n=16 features in 8 pairs -> m=4 dims (80 params), importance-weighted MSE, Adam lr=0.01, 3000 online steps, batch 1024, density fixed at p=0.1, 2 seeds. Three independent within-pair knobs, each an exact mixture construction verified empirically in-run (emp corr within 0.008 of target): (i) INDICATOR correlation rho via the sibling's shared-coin mixture; (ii) VALUE correlation c via a copy/mirror mixture - with prob |c| the partner's value is copied (c>0) or mirrored v2=1-v1 (c<0) from the first member's Uniform[0,1] draw, else independent, so marginals stay uniform and the Pearson correlation of co-active values is exactly c; (iii) IMPORTANCE ratio r with importances (2/(1+r), 2r/(1+r)) so the pair's TOTAL importance is 2 for every r - r is a pure split knob, not a pair-weight knob. Three sweeps, 33 distinct cells / 66 runs (shared cells trained once): A importance r in {1,2,4,8,16,64,256} x rho in {0, 0.75, 1} at c=0, where rho=0 is the UNCORRELATED CONTROL separating merge-abandonment from ordinary low-importance feature dropping; B value correlation c in {+1,+0.5,0,-0.5,-1} x rho in {0.75,1} at r=1; C joint corner r in {1,4,16} x c in {+1,0,-1} at rho=1. Per cell: the sibling's merge metric (mean within-pair |cos| among pairs where BOTH members have ||W_i|| >= 0.5) plus SIGNED cosine, a per-pair classification into MERGED (|cos|>=0.7) / AMBIGUOUS / LOCALLY-ORTHOGONAL (|cos|<=0.3) / DROPPED, column norms, cross-pair |cos|, and held-out per-feature reconstruction MSE on a fresh 8192-sample batch normalised by that feature's variance (1.0 = no better than the best constant predictor).
architecture: linear tied W (4x16) + bias, ReLU output, importance-weighted MSE (~80 params)

task: sparse feature reconstruction (toy superposition)
compute: CPU single-threaded, 390s for all 33 cells / 66 training runs

metrics.headline: no correlated pair EVER chose local orthogonality (0 of 240 pair-instances across 30 correlated cells); unequal importance is answered by amplitude decay along the SAME direction (|cos| pinned at 0.999 while the weak member's ||W|| falls 0.714 -> 0.014 over r=1..64, no breakpoint to r=256) and anticorrelated values only bend the merge to |cos| 0.750 (rho=1) / 0.636 (rho=0.75); co-occurrence subsidises the weak feature by roughly a 16x importance discount

result_summary: The hypothesis is REFUTED on the importance axis and only partially met on the value axis; the honest headline is that MERGING SURVIVES ESSENTIALLY EVERYTHING. (1) NO PAIR EVER CHOOSES LOCAL ORTHOGONALITY. Across all 30 correlated cells (rho >= 0.75), zero of 240 pair-instances landed in the orthogonal bin (|cos| <= 0.3); the minimum within-pair |cos| over every surviving correlated pair is 0.636, about 50 degrees, not 90. The only cells that ever produce orthogonal pairs are the rho=0 uncorrelated control (0.25 of pairs at r=1), which is exactly what the control exists to distinguish. (2) UNEQUAL IMPORTANCE DOES NOT BEND THE MERGE - IT FADES THE WEAK MEMBER ALONG THE SAME DIRECTION. Whenever both members survive, |cos| is 0.999, identically at r=1, 2 and 4; there is no intermediate geometry, the metric simply becomes undefined when the weak member drops below the norm threshold. The mechanism is in the norms: at rho=1 the weak member's ||W|| decays 0.714 -> 0.613 -> 0.495 -> 0.278 -> 0.098 -> 0.014 across r=1..64 while the strong member's grows 0.716 -> 1.008. breakpoint_importance_ratio is null at both rho=0.75 and rho=1 up to a 256x importance ratio. So a polysemantic direction degrades CONTINUOUSLY into a single-feature direction rather than splitting. (3) MERGING IS A SUBSIDY, AND THE CONTROL SIZES IT. Weak-member held-out NMSE (1.0 = the constant-predictor floor) at r=4 is 1.001 at rho=0 - the uncorrelated low-importance feature is completely unrepresented - but 0.634 at rho=0.75 and 0.326 at rho=1. Riding a stronger partner's direction is worth roughly a 16x importance discount: rho=1 at r=16 (0.861) is about as well reconstructed as rho=0 at r ~ 1-2, and the co-occurring weak feature is only fully dead by r ~ 64. For interpretability this is the uncomfortable part: a direction can carry a real, recoverable second feature at 1/16 the importance with NO angular signature that it is doing so. (4) ANTICORRELATED VALUES ARE THE ONLY STRESSOR THAT MOVES THE ANGLE, AND IT STALLS. Within-pair |cos| falls monotonically as c goes +1 -> -1: 1.000 / 1.000 / 0.999 / 0.933 / 0.750 at rho=1 and 1.000 / 0.999 / 0.999 / 0.688 / 0.636 at rho=0.75. The sole 0.7-crossing in the experiment is rho=0.75, c=-0.5 (0.688) - and it is a partial rotation, not a split: the classification goes merged -> AMBIGUOUS (0.31 merged / 0.69 ambiguous / 0.00 orthogonal at rho=0.75, c=-1). Signed cosine EQUALS |cos| everywhere (+0.750 at rho=1, c=-1), so anticorrelated VALUES do not produce the antipodal geometry that anticorrelated CO-OCCURRENCE does in Anthropic's vignettes - non-negative values still need positive projection onto a shared axis. And the response is global rather than local: cross-pair |cos| rises 0.146 -> 0.334 as within-pair |cos| falls, i.e. the whole arrangement decompresses instead of the pair reorganising, even though the cost of merging rises 5.7x (NMSE 0.057 -> 0.324). (5) THE TWO STRESSORS TOGETHER PUSH TOWARD DROPPING, NOT SPLITTING: at rho=1, r=16 with c=+1 (merging lossless) every pair stays perfectly merged and alive, while at r=4, c=-1 the weak member is already 100% dropped against 0.50 alive at r=4, c=0. CAVEATS, worst first: one density (p=0.1) and one geometry (16->4), and the sibling showed the merge ONSET moves with density so the breakpoint may too; 2 seeds; the represented (||W|| >= 0.5) and merge/ortho (0.7/0.3) cutoffs are thresholds, which is why norms and per-feature NMSE are reported as continuous companions to every classification; 3000 steps with no per-cell convergence check; and only one within-pair value-coupling family (the copy/mirror mixture) was tested.

novelty_check.conclusion: Partial prior art on every ingredient, none on the combination. Anthropic's Toy Models of Superposition (transformer-circuits 2022 / arXiv:2209.10652) has both a feature-importance axis and a correlated/anticorrelated-features section, but sweeps them separately, reports geometry qualitatively, and its 'anticorrelated' means anticorrelated CO-OCCURRENCE rather than anticorrelated values within a co-occurring pair. arXiv:2603.09972 (From Data Statistics to Feature Geometry, fetched and read in full) studies how correlations shape superposition geometry but on BINARY bag-of-words features from WikiText-103, so it has no value-magnitude axis at all, no importance-ratio sweep, and no within-pair cosine breakpoint metric. arXiv:2605.28149 (Sign-Aware Gated SAEs) models anticorrelated features on the SAE side, downstream of this question. What is new here: crossing the two stressors against the sibling run's merge metric with a NORMALISED importance split (pair total importance held constant so r is a pure split knob), an uncorrelated rho=0 CONTROL that separates merge-abandonment from ordinary low-importance feature dropping, an explicit separation of VALUE correlation from INDICATOR correlation as independent axes, and per-feature held-out loss normalised against the constant-predictor floor. The 'co-occurrence is worth roughly a 16x importance discount' number and the amplitude-decay-not-rotation mechanism are, to this search, not stated quantitatively anywhere. Search was web-only (arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this box); the one 2026-dated arXiv hit was read directly rather than leaned on for numbers.
novelty_check.note: Anthropic's paper does report that low-importance features get dropped and that correlated features can collapse together; the quantitative crossing of the two, the control, and the subsidy magnitude are the contribution.

title: Echo State Network on Mackey-Glass-17: there is no edge-of-chaos ridge just below sr=1 - the free-running optimum sits ABOVE 1 in 13 of 16 reservoirs (median sr 1.10), the sr=0.9 default costs 7.3x the error, and the memory-capacity peak is too flat to localise it
hypothesis: The classic 'edge of chaos' claim predicts a sharp performance ridge just below spectral radius 1: NRMSE on Mackey-Glass-17 should fall steeply as sr approaches 1 from below, be minimised in a narrow band around sr ~ 0.9-1.0, degrade quickly past sr = 1, and the NRMSE optimum should coincide with the peak of linear memory capacity.
question: On the classic MG-17 benchmark, is the spectral-radius/performance curve of an Echo State Network actually a sharp ridge just below sr=1, or is the optimum broad, displaced, or set by something other than the nominal spectral radius - and does the NRMSE optimum coincide with the linear memory-capacity peak?
method: Hand-rolled ESN in numpy, no reservoirpy and no gradient training of any kind: x[t] = tanh(W x[t-1] + W_in u[t] + b) with leak rate 1.0, sparse W (density 0.1, entries U(-1,1)) rescaled to a target spectral radius sr, W_in and b ~ U(-1,1)*input_scaling, and the ONLY learned object a linear readout yhat[t+1] = [1, u[t], x[t]] . W_out fitted in closed form by ridge regression. Data: Mackey-Glass tau=17 (dx/dt = 0.2 x(t-17)/(1+x(t-17)^10) - 0.1 x(t)) integrated by RK4 at dt=0.1 with the delayed term held over the step, subsampled to unit time step, 1000 unit-steps of transient discarded, squashed by tanh(x-1) (Jaeger's standard MG-17 ESN preprocessing); the series is deterministic (constant history x=1.2) so every arm sees the identical signal. Splits 200 washout / 3000 train / 1000 val / 2000 test. FOUR METRICS: (1) teacher-forced 1-step test NRMSE; (2) the classic MG-17 free-running NRMSE at horizon 84 - the readout's own output is fed back as the next input for 84 steps from 50 evenly spaced test start points (reservoir state taken from the teacher-forced pass), squared error read at step 84 only, normalised by the test signal's std; (3) valid prediction time, the first free-running step where |error| > 0.2 * std; (4) linear memory capacity MC = sum_k r^2(k) for k = 1..N, measured on a SEPARATE i.i.d. uniform drive rescaled to have the MG signal's std, with a states-only (no current input) ridge readout, r^2 evaluated on a held-out slice. SWEEP: sr over 30 values from 0.30 to 1.60 (0.05 spacing, refined to 0.025 on [0.90, 1.05]) x 5 arms x their seeds = 16 independent reservoirs and 480 cells: N200/input_scaling 0.5 (5 seeds, headline), N100/0.5 (3), N400/0.5 (2), N200/0.1 (3), N200/1.0 (3). CONTROLS: the recurrent topology is drawn ONCE per (N, seed) and only rescaled by sr, so the sweep is strictly within-reservoir; the input-scaling arms reuse the identical topologies (paired comparison of the drive effect); the MC probe reuses the same i.i.d. sequence across arms; and the ridge coefficient alpha is re-selected on the validation split for EVERY cell from a 6-point grid 1e-10..1, separately for the 1-step metric (val 1-step NRMSE) and for the free-running metric (val NRMSE@84 over 20 val rollouts), so no point on the sr curve can be an artifact of a regulariser tuned at a single sr. Sharpness is quantified as the fraction of the swept sr range whose mean metric is within 1.5x of the optimum.
architecture: Echo State Network (fixed random recurrent reservoir + ridge-regression linear readout), N in {100, 200, 400} tanh units, sparse recurrent matrix at density 0.1, leak rate 1.0; trainable parameters = the readout only (N+2 weights, i.e. 102/202/402), reservoir weights are never updated

dataset.name: Mackey-Glass tau=17 chaotic time series (MG-17), RK4 dt=0.1 subsampled to unit step, tanh(x-1) squashing; plus an i.i.d. uniform drive for the memory-capacity probe
dataset.source: generated in run.py (delay differential equation, deterministic constant history x=1.2, 1000 unit-steps of transient discarded; 6289 points used)

task: chaotic time-series prediction: 1-step-ahead and 84-step free-running (generative) prediction, plus a linear memory-capacity probe
compute: CPU single-threaded, 409.6s (6.8 min) for the full 480-cell sweep; no gradient training; two back-to-back runs produced byte-identical results.json apart from duration_sec

metrics.reproducibility: two back-to-back runs produced byte-identical results.json apart from duration_sec

result_summary: The hypothesis is REFUTED on location and only half-confirmed on sharpness. (1) THE OPTIMUM IS ABOVE sr=1, NOT BELOW. At the headline arm (N=200, input scaling 0.5) the free-running NRMSE@84 minimum sits at sr = 1.10 (0.01183) and the 1-step minimum at sr = 1.15. Across all 16 independent (size, seed) reservoirs the per-seed argmin of NRMSE@84 has median 1.10 and range [0.95, 1.30], with 13 of 16 strictly above 1 and 14 of 16 at or above 1. The conventional 'set sr just under 1' default is measurably expensive: sr = 0.90 costs 7.34x the error of the optimum (0.0868 vs 0.0118) and sr = 0.95 costs 6.44x. (2) THE CURVE IS A RAMP AND A CLIFF, NOT A RESONANCE PEAK. Below the optimum NRMSE@84 falls smoothly and monotonically across the entire subcritical range (0.962 at sr=0.30 -> 0.0118 at sr=1.10, an 81x improvement) with no knee - the largest single-grid-step improvement below the optimum is only 1.98x. Above the optimum it collapses abruptly: 3.72x degradation across one 0.05 step (sr 1.25 -> 1.30) and 73.5x the best error by sr=1.60. The 'sharp ridge' people remember is the supercritical cliff, and it sits past the optimum, not just below sr=1. (3) 'SHARP' IS A PROPERTY OF THE METRIC, NOT THE RESERVOIR. The band within 1.5x of the best covers only 10% of the swept sr range for NRMSE@84 at N=200 (6.7% at N=400) - genuinely sharp - but 33% for 1-step prediction (sr in [0.925, 1.25]), and valid-prediction-time is saturated at the full 84 steps everywhere in sr in [1.025, 1.20]. Ask a short-memory question and the ridge disappears into a plateau. (4) THE INPUT DRIVE SETS WHERE THE RIDGE IS, WHICH IS THE MECHANISM. At fixed N=200 the NRMSE@84 optimum is at sr = 1.00 for input scaling 0.1, 1.10 for 0.5 and 1.05 for 1.0, and the tolerance for supercritical sr grows sharply with drive: at sr = 1.40 the error is 14.0x the best at drive 0.1 but only 2.69x at drive 1.0. The memory-capacity peak moves monotonically and much more cleanly with drive: sr = 1.00 (drive 0.1), 1.20 (0.5), 1.35 (1.0), with peak MC falling 39.9 -> 22.8 -> 17.0. This is exactly what tanh saturation predicts - the effective local gain at the operating point is below the nominal linear spectral radius, so the harder the drive, the further above 1 sr must go for the same effective gain - and in the weak-drive limit the classic boundary reappears exactly (optimum = 1.000 for all three seeds). (5) MEMORY CAPACITY IS A BAD GUIDE TO THE TASK OPTIMUM IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. Its peak is displaced from the NRMSE@84 optimum by +0.10 (N=200), +0.075 (N=100), -0.05 (N=400), 0.00 (weak drive) and +0.30 (strong drive), and it is far too flat to localise anything: 63% of the sweep is within 1.5x of peak MC versus 10% for NRMSE@84. The sharpest illustration is that at N=200, sr = 1.40 retains 83.8% of peak memory capacity while free-running error is already 22.5x worse than at the optimum - MC gives no warning about the cliff that actually destroys the prediction. (6) SANITY: zero divergences in 480 cells / 24,000 free-running rollouts; best NRMSE@84 = 0.00243 at N=400, in the right ballpark for a classic MG-17 ESN of that size; bigger is monotonically better (0.0859 / 0.0118 / 0.00243 at N = 100 / 200 / 400) and the curve's shape is size-invariant while its optimum drifts right with N (1.025 / 1.10 / 1.25). CAVEATS, worst first: ONE Mackey-Glass realisation and one test set (the series is deterministic, so the sr curves are properly paired but the absolute numbers carry no data-sampling error bar); only 2 seeds at N=400 and 3 at N=100; leak rate (1.0), density (0.1) and horizon (84) each fixed at one value, so this is a 2-D slice (sr x input scaling) of a larger space; no state noise during training - the classic stabiliser for generative mode - here replaced by the per-cell validation-selected ridge alpha; MC is measured on an i.i.d. drive, a different input distribution from the task, which is standard practice but means the two x-axes are only loosely comparable; and 'input scaling' scales W_in and the bias together. The obvious next run is to measure mean |tanh'| at the operating point and re-plot every curve against that EFFECTIVE gain instead of sr - the prediction is that the five arms' optima collapse onto one point.

novelty_check.conclusion: Replication, not novelty. The central finding is already established in the specialist reservoir-computing literature even though the folk form of the claim ('tune sr to just below 1, that is the edge of chaos') persists: Carroll (arXiv:2012.01409, Chaos 2020) asks 'Do Reservoir Computers Work Best at the Edge of Chaos?' and answers no on Lorenz/Rossler-type signals; Carroll (Chaos 32, 023123, 2022) shows the memory optimum and the task optimum are different points; Yildiz, Jaeger & Kiebel (Neural Networks 2012) show sr < 1 is neither necessary nor sufficient for the echo state property; and both Lukosevicius' Practical Guide and the Lukosevicius-Jaeger 2009 survey state outright that sr > 1 can be optimal for tasks with short memory requirements and that input scaling co-determines the operating regime. Jaeger 2001 is the origin of the MG-17 free-running-84 benchmark itself. Two things we did not find combined in prior work and that are the only additions here: (i) a paired input-scaling arm run on IDENTICAL reservoir topologies, isolating the drive-dependence of the optimum's location and of the MC peak (1.00 / 1.20 / 1.35 as drive goes 0.1 / 0.5 / 1.0) as a single controlled sweep; and (ii) a per-cell validation-selected ridge alpha, which rules out the most common confound in published sr sweeps - a regulariser tuned once at one sr. We also quantify 'how sharp' rather than asserting it (fraction of the swept range within 1.5x of the optimum: 10% for the 84-step metric, 33% for 1-step, 63% for memory capacity). Search was web-only; arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this box.

title: SAEs on the merged-pair toy model: the dictionary recovers all 8 MERGED pair-directions one-to-one and 0 of the 16 true features (max member-selectivity 0.007/1.0 across 27 SAEs) - but an MLP probe reads the within-pair difference at R2 0.47 from the same 4 numbers, so the SAE's ceiling is its linear hypothesis class, not lost information
hypothesis: An L1 SAE trained on the 4-dim hidden layer of the merged-pair toy model recovers the 8 MERGED pair-directions, not the 16 true generative features, and no SAE feature can separate the two members of a merged pair because the model's hidden layer no longer contains that information (a probe on the 4-dim hidden cannot predict the within-pair value difference).
question: When the ground truth is a KNOWN merged representation - a toy model that provably put each correlated feature pair on ONE shared direction - does a small L1 SAE recover the 8 merged pair-directions or the 16 true generative features, and is the failure to reach 16 an information-theoretic ceiling or a hypothesis-class ceiling?
method: Two-stage, both stages trained here. STAGE 1, the answer key: retrain the toy autoencoder of 2026-07-23_superposition-correlation-phase unchanged - x_hat = ReLU(W^T W x + b) with W of shape 4x16, i.e. n=16 features in 8 pairs -> m=4 hidden dims (80 params), Adam lr 0.01, 3000 online steps, batch 1024, MSE. Data: per sample per pair, with probability rho both members share ONE Bernoulli(p) on/off coin else independent coins (within-pair indicator correlation exactly rho); active values are ALWAYS independent Uniform[0,1], so a merged pair still carries two independent numbers and merging is genuinely lossy. Five toy models: primary rho=1.0/p=0.10 x seeds {0,1}, plus rho=0.75/p=0.10, rho=1.0/p=0.05, and an UNMERGED positive control rho=0.0/p=0.10. Merging is verified per arm (within-pair |cos| >= 0.95) BEFORE any SAE is trained. STAGE 2: activations h = W x on FRESH seeded data drawn from a different generator stream than training (65536 train / 32768 held-out eval), scaled so E||h|| = sqrt(m) to make lambda comparable across arms. 45 standard ReLU SAEs, f = ReLU((h - b_dec) W_enc + b_enc), h_hat = f W_dec + b_dec, unit-norm decoder rows renormalised every step, L1 on f, dead-feature resampling at 40%/70%, Adam lr 3e-3, batch 512, 4000 steps: expansion 2x/4x/8x (8/16/32 dictionary features over a 4-dim space) x lambda in {0.02, 0.06, 0.2} x 5 model arms. TWO ANSWER KEYS from the same trained W: KEY-8 = the 8 merged pair-directions (top left singular vector of each pair's 2-column block); KEY-16 = the 16 true generative directions (unit columns of W). Scoring adds four things the usual max-cosine score lacks: (1) SIGNED cosine (feature values are non-negative so a feature pushes h along +W_i); (2) GREEDY INJECTIVE matching so one SAE feature cannot be credited with recovering both members of a pair whose unit columns are the same vector to 2.6 degrees; (3) a RANDOM-UNIT-DIRECTION NULL, 400 trials at every alive-count, which is large in R^4 (a random direction lands within cos >= 0.9 of a fixed target 1.9% of the time, so 32 random directions already 'recover' 3.6 of 8 pair-directions) - all headline numbers therefore use cos >= 0.95, with the 0.9/0.95/0.99 curves in results.json; (4) a FUNCTIONAL criterion - correlate each alive SAE feature's activation with every true feature value and compute the member imbalance |r_a - r_b|/(|r_a| + |r_b|) on the pair it is most associated with (0 = responds to both members identically, i.e. a pair feature; 1 = a true single-feature detector); a true feature counts as functionally recovered only if some SAE feature is BOTH directionally matched (cos >= 0.95) AND member-selective (imbalance >= 0.5). THE DECISIVE CONTROL: linear ridge and 2x64 ReLU-MLP probes from the 4-dim hidden onto, per pair, x_a, x_b, their SUM and their DIFFERENCE (restricted to co-active samples) plus 'which member fired' on exactly-one-active samples, 70/30 split, R2 against the masked-mean baseline - with two nulls, an EXACT-MERGE ORACLE (rebuild h after projecting each pair's two columns onto their exactly shared direction: the reference for 'the information really is gone') and a SHUFFLED-h null (the probe's own optimism floor).
architecture: Anthropic-style toy autoencoder ReLU(W^T W x + b), W 4x16, 80 params; plus 45 ReLU+L1 sparse autoencoders over the 4-dim hidden layer with 8/16/32 dictionary features (~70-290 params each); plus linear-ridge and 2x64 MLP probes

dataset.name: synthetic sparse features in 8 correlated pairs (16 features), and the 4-dim hidden activations of the toy model trained on them
dataset.source: generated in run.py (recipe of 2026-07-23_superposition-correlation-phase; SAE/probe data drawn from a separate seeded generator stream)

task: sparse-feature reconstruction under 4x compression (toy model), then dictionary learning on the compressed representation scored against two competing ground-truth feature sets
compute: CPU single-threaded, 447s (7.5 min) for 5 toy models + 15 probe fits + 45 SAEs + 5600 random-direction null trials; two back-to-back runs reproduced every headline metric exactly (only per-cell wall-clock fields differ)

metrics.bijection_setting: 2x lambda=0.2 (8 dictionary features), 8/8 pair-directions in BOTH seeds, max_feats_per_pairdir = 1
metrics.reproducibility: two back-to-back runs reproduced every headline metric exactly; only per-cell wall-clock fields differ

result_summary: The hypothesis is CONFIRMED on the SAE half and REFUTED on the mechanism half, and the refutation is the more interesting half. (1) THE SAE FINDS 8, NEVER 16. On the primary merged arm (within-pair |cos| 0.999 vs cross-pair 0.155, merge verified before scoring) the best setting recovers 8 of 8 merged pair-directions (4x, lambda=0.06, seed 1; FVU 0.00021, L0 2.06, 0% dead) against a random-direction null of 0.83 (p95 = 2). The cleanest cell is 2x, lambda=0.2 - an 8-feature dictionary over a 4-dim space - which hits 8/8 in BOTH seeds with exactly one dictionary feature per pair-direction and no duplicates: a bijection. And 0 of 16 true features are FUNCTIONALLY recovered in all 27 SAEs across all three merged arms; not one merged-arm SAE contains a single member-selective feature. The best setting's maximum member imbalance over its whole dictionary is 0.0069 (mean 0.0033) on a 0-1 scale where the unmerged control reaches 1.0000. (2) THE '16 TRUE FEATURES' SCORE IS A MIRAGE, WHICH IS THE METHODOLOGICAL FINDING. Scored naively by max cosine against the generative feature list, the SAE appears to recover up to 15 of 16 true features (rho=0.75, 8x, lambda=0.2; 13/16 on the primary arm) - 94% recovery of features the representation demonstrably does not separately encode. Every extra match is a DUPLICATE: no merged SAE ever claims more than 8 distinct pair-directions, with up to 7 alive features piled onto one direction, and injective matching does not stop it because with 32 features and 8 real directions there are plenty of near-copies to assign to the two (identical-to-2.6-degrees) members of a pair. Only the functional selectivity test separates the two answer keys, and it says 8/0, not 8/12. (3) SPARSITY IS THE KNOB, WIDTH IS NOT. lambda 0.02 -> 0.2 is worth +4 to +5 pair-directions at every expansion (2x: 4.0 -> 8.0; 4x: 2.0 -> 7.5; 8x: 2.0 -> 7.0) and is the only knob that ever reaches 8/8; the widest dictionary is the worst at every lambda while inflating the FALSE KEY-16 score from 8.0 to 12.0. FVU spans 0.0000-0.0065 across all 45 SAEs - every one reconstructs the 4-dim space essentially perfectly - so reconstruction quality carries ZERO signal about which answer key is being recovered, exactly as in the grokked-model sibling. The right dictionary size turned out to be the number of directions the model USES (8), not the number of features the data HAS (16). (4) THE CONTROL OVERTURNS THE 'INFORMATION IS GONE' HALF. The within-pair distinction is destroyed LINEARLY but not absolutely. A linear probe on the 4-dim hidden reads the within-pair difference at R2 = 0.034 in the merged model versus 0.299 in the unmerged control (9x gap) while reading the SUM at 0.588 - so a linear dictionary genuinely cannot represent the distinction, which is exactly why the SAE's ceiling is 8. But an MLP probe reads the same difference at R2 = 0.473 from the same 4 numbers. The exact-merge oracle proves where that signal lives: collapse each pair onto its EXACTLY shared direction and the same probe drops to 0.023 (shuffled-h floor -0.023) while the sum survives at 0.750. The residual 2.56-degree splay is carrying it. Dose-response confirms this: the p=0.05 arm merged less completely (|cos| 0.9375, two pairs at 0.80/0.71) and its MLP difference-R2 is correspondingly higher at 0.736. At rho=0.75 even 'which member fired, on samples where exactly one did' is linearly undecodable (-0.003) but nonlinearly decodable at 0.477. So the SAE's failure to reach 16 is a HYPOTHESIS-CLASS ceiling (linear dictionary + sparsity prior), not an information-theoretic one. (5) EVERY CONTROL LANDS WHERE IT SHOULD. The unmerged rho=0 arm reaches member imbalance 1.0000 with 3-17 member-selective features per SAE and functionally recovers up to 2 true features, while recovering only 0-2 of the (non-existent) 8 pair-directions - so neither metric is pinned to its floor by construction and the merged arms' 0.0069 and 0/16 are real zeros. The random-direction null is reported at every alive-count and is large enough to matter (0.37 -> 1.47 pair-directions at cos >= 0.95, 1.15 -> 3.56 at cos >= 0.9), which is why cos >= 0.9 backs no headline claim. CAVEATS, worst first: two seeds on the primary arm and one on each of the other three, and the seed spread is real (seed 0 killed one member of two pairs, ||W|| 0.023/0.031, leaving 14/16 represented and 6 merged pairs, and had a 25x larger max member imbalance, 0.35 vs 0.007); one geometry (16->4) and one merge mechanism (indicator correlation at equal importance); the 0.95 cosine bar and the 0.5 imbalance bar are judgement calls made before scoring, which is why the full cos {0.9,0.95,0.99} curves and continuous imbalance values are in results.json; the MLP probe is one architecture at one budget so 0.473 is a LOWER bound on nonlinear decodability; only one SAE family (ReLU + L1) - no top-k, JumpReLU or gated variants; and the p=0.05 arm did not fully merge (mean |cos| 0.9375) so it is reported as a partial-merge data point, not a replicate.

novelty_check.conclusion: Partial prior art. The core phenomenon is known: Evan Anders' 'Sparse autoencoders find composed features in small toy models' (2024) is the nearest neighbour and reports that SAEs on correlated toy features learn composed rather than individual features; 'Feature Hedging' (arXiv:2505.11756) shows correlated features make narrow SAEs mix directions (mechanism on the SAE side rather than in the model's own geometry); SynthSAEBench (arXiv:2602.14687) and 'Are Sparse Autoencoder Benchmarks Reliable?' (arXiv:2605.18229) build synthetic-ground-truth SAE evaluations including correlation as a factor; 'On the Limits of Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2506.15963) gives theory for what L1 SAEs can identify; the toy model and its correlated-feature merging come from Toy Models of Superposition (arXiv:2209.10652) and the SAE recipe from ARENA 3.1 / Towards Monosemanticity. Four things we did not find in prior work and that are the additions here: (i) scoring an SAE against TWO explicit competing answer keys derived from the SAME trained W (the 8 merged directions vs the 16 generative features) so 'which ground truth did it find' is a measurement rather than an interpretation; (ii) a random-direction NULL for the recovery statistic itself, reported at every alive-count, in the low-dimensional space where that null is large (3.56 of 8 'recovered' by 32 random directions at cos >= 0.9); (iii) the DUPLICATE-MATCH ARTIFACT quantified - up to 15/16 true features 'recovered' by max cosine while the dictionary claims only 8 distinct directions, which is a concrete failure mode for any synthetic-feature-list SAE benchmark; and (iv) the EXACT-MERGE ORACLE probe, which separates 'the SAE cannot find it' from 'the information is gone' and is what refuted half of our own hypothesis (linear R2 0.034 vs MLP 0.473 vs oracle 0.023). The toy model, the merging behaviour and the SAE recipe are replications; the evaluation protocol and the linear-vs-nonlinear ceiling result are the contribution. title: Validation-based clause pruning un-buries the planted DNF: at 20% label noise a 500-sample NOISY validation set restores Tsetlin clause precision 0.49 -> 1.00 with zero recall loss, and the binding constraint is the unknown noise rate, not the missing clean labels
hypothesis: Scoring each learned Tsetlin clause by its individual precision on a held-out validation set drawn from the same NOISY distribution, and pruning the low-precision clauses, restores clause precision to ~1.0 on the noise-buried rule set of 2026-07-24 at eps=0.2 without hurting exact recall or accuracy; at eps=0.3, where recall was already degraded to 0.556, pruning either helps or amputates the surviving true clauses.
question: Can post-hoc, label-noise-blind clause pruning/weighting separate the planted clauses from the spurious noise-fitted ones that bury them in a Tsetlin Machine, and at what noise level does that separation fail?
method: Reuse the pure-numpy Tsetlin Machine and planted 3-clause DNF generator of 2026-07-24_tsetlin-dnf-recovery verbatim (identical rng streams; baselines reproduce that run exactly, max abs diff 0.0 over 12 matched runs). Train 20-clause TMs (T=10, s=3.0, 60 epochs, 3000 samples) at label-flip eps in {0.0, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4} x 3 seeds. Score every clause on a held-out validation set drawn from the SAME noisy distribution (n in {100, 500, 2000}) by coverage and validation precision P(y=polarity | clause fires). Compare three treatments: (a) a 51-point pruning-threshold sweep (oracle upper bound), (b) a naive oracle-free rule keeping clauses within 0.95x the best clause precision, (c) a Wilson rule that estimates the unknown precision ceiling 1-eps as the largest Wilson lower bound over well-covered clauses and keeps every clause whose Wilson upper bound reaches it; plus a soft weighting variant. Re-measure clause precision, exact clause recall, mean best Jaccard, clean test accuracy, functional accuracy over all 1024 inputs, soundness of kept clauses, and DNF read-off accuracy.
architecture: vanilla two-class Tsetlin Machine, 20 clauses x 20 literals (400 automata), pure numpy, no gradients; post-hoc clause scoring/pruning/weighting on top

metrics.headline: at eps=0.2 an oracle-free pruning rule scored on 500 NOISY validation labels restores clause precision 0.486 -> 1.000 with exact recall untouched at 1.0 and the read-off DNF functionally perfect (0.643 -> 1.000); at eps=0.3 it never amputates (recall stays 0.556) and reaches precision 1.0 given 2000 validation samples; at eps=0.4 nothing separates (0.067)

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed at eps=0.2, partially at eps=0.3, refuted at eps=0.4 - and the real obstacle is the unknown noise rate, not the absence of clean labels. Because a logically sound clause's validation precision concentrates at 1-eps, the useful pruning thresholds form a narrow band just below 1-eps. A naive 'keep clauses within 0.95x of the best' rule AMPUTATES (eps=0.2: precision 1.0 but exact recall 1.0 -> 0.444, accuracy 0.937 -> 0.820) because a lucky low-coverage clause sets the ceiling too high; replacing the raw max with a Wilson lower bound over clauses covering >=5% of the validation set fixes it exactly. That rule takes eps=0.2 from clause precision 0.486 to 1.000 with zero recall loss in all 3 seeds - the surviving positive clauses are exactly the 3 planted ones and reading them off as a DNF is functionally perfect (0.643 -> 1.000). At eps=0.3 pruning never removes a planted clause that training kept (recall stays 0.556) and reaches precision 1.0 with 2000 validation samples (0.34 with 500). At eps=0.4 the signal is gone (precision 0.067; best oracle threshold only 0.667). Cost: pruning both polarities unbalances the vote, so the pruned TM loses ~4.7 accuracy points at eps=0.2 (0.937 -> 0.890) even though the oracle threshold tau=0.74 gives precision 1.0 AND accuracy 0.978; soft weighting instead of pruning is safer but weaker (weight mass on planted clauses 0.667 -> 0.858, never a clean list). Baselines reproduce 2026-07-24 exactly (max abs diff 0.0).

title: Modern Hopfield capacity at d=64 is exponential in d with the textbook constant (0.244 bits/dim, R2=0.993) but stops responding to beta above 1 - the update is just a nearest-neighbour decoder, and corruption, not temperature, is the binding constraint
hypothesis: The modern (continuous, softmax) Hopfield update xi <- X^T softmax(beta X xi) of Ramsauer et al. (arXiv:2008.02217) has capacity exponential in d, so at d=64 it retrieves corrupted queries from banks of thousands of random bipolar patterns - far past the classical Hebbian 0.14d ~ 9 - with a sharp retrieval boundary that moves outward as the inverse temperature beta grows, and at low beta retrieval collapses to metastable averages of many stored patterns.
question: What is the EMPIRICAL exact-retrieval capacity of a modern Hopfield associative memory on a joint (beta x corruption x N x d) grid, how does it compare to the classical Hebbian rule on identical pattern banks, and where does the metastable-averaging regime actually begin?
method: Hand-rolled, training-free numpy. Stored patterns X (N x d bipolar); modern update xi <- X^T softmax(beta X xi) iterated up to 10 steps or until max|dxi| < 1e-6, with the 1-step state recorded separately; classical reference W = X^T X / d with zero diagonal and 5 asynchronous random-order sign sweeps. Queries flip exactly round(f*d) components of a stored pattern, 500 queries per cell, nested RNG so every beta sees byte-identical queries. Exact retrieval = sign(xi_final) matches the true pattern in ALL d components; empirical capacity = largest N on a half-octave grid such that every swept N' <= N still clears 95% (first-crossing; the generous 'largest N anywhere above 95%' is also stored). Four sweeps: (1) d=64, N=2..4096 half-octave, beta in {0.25,1,4,16}, f in {0.1,0.2,0.3,0.4}, with the f=0.2 slice extended to N=65536; (2) classical Hebbian on the same banks (N<=256); (3) dimension sweep d in {16,24,32,40,48} at f=0.2, beta in {4,16}, with the d=64 point supplied by sweep 1 (same protocol, different bank - the only slice swept deep enough to be uncensored); (4) 1752 unique binarized 8x8 sklearn digits at d=64. Diagnostics per cell: cosine overlap, Hamming error, softmax participation ratio 1/sum(p^2), fixed-point norm ||xi||/sqrt(d), softmax argmax accuracy, and the query's nearest-neighbour margin.
architecture: modern (continuous, softmax-based) Hopfield network, no learned parameters - the memory IS the pattern matrix; classical Hebbian outer-product Hopfield as the reference

metrics.headline: d=64, f=0.2, iterated: empirical capacity (largest N with >=95% exact retrieval) = beta 0.25: 2048, beta 1.0: 65536, beta 4.0: 65536, beta 16.0: 32768; classical Hebbian: 6 (0.14d = 9.0). capacity at f=0.3: beta 0.25: 64, beta 1.0: 64, beta 4.0: 64, beta 16.0: 64; at f=0.4: beta 0.25: 0, beta 1.0: 0, beta 4.0: 0, beta 16.0: 0

result_summary: Split verdict. CONFIRMED: capacity is exponential in d with the textbook constant - log2(capacity) vs d over d=16,24,32,40,48,64 at f=0.2 is linear at 0.244 bits/dim (R2=0.993) at beta=16 and 0.257 bits/dim (R2=0.963) at beta=4, within 6% of the random-code prediction (1-2f)^2/(2 ln 2)=0.2597; at d=64, f=0.2 the empirical capacity is >=65536 (censored, 96.6% exact retrieval at the largest bank swept) versus 6 for the classical Hebbian rule on the identical bank (theory 0.14d=9), a ~10^4x gap. REFUTED: the boundary does not move with beta above 1. At f=0.3 all four temperatures give exactly the same capacity (64) and at f=0.2 beta=16 is marginally worse than beta=4, because for beta>=1 the exact-retrieval curve sits on top of the nearest-neighbour-decoder curve (0.966 vs 0.944 at N=65536, the gap being integer-overlap ties) - the softmax adds nothing over 'snap to the closest stored pattern'. Beta is a floor, not a dial: the only visible beta effect is a 32x jump between 0.25 and 1. The binding constraint is corruption, not temperature or N: d=64 holds >=65536 patterns at f=0.2, 64 at f=0.3, and fewer than 2 at f=0.4 (a two-pattern memory completes only 91.8% of 40%-corrupted queries). Metastability CONFIRMED and sharp: at beta=0.25 retrieval goes 0.996 (N=2048) -> 0.004 (N=2896) in one half-octave, after which the softmax participation ratio reaches 784 effective patterns and the fixed point has 0.005*sqrt(d) norm and cosine 0.005 to the truth - but the true pattern is STILL the softmax argmax for 96.8% of queries, identical to beta=16, so the collapse is a readout failure with the memory intact; iterating makes it worse (1-step capacity 2896 vs iterated 2048) because each step shrinks the state norm and hence the effective temperature. Correlated real patterns (binarized 8x8 digits, mean |cos| 0.487 vs 0.100 random) lose nearly everything: capacity 128-181 at f=0.1 and never above 95% past N=11 at f=0.2.

novelty_check.conclusion: The exponential-capacity theorem (Ramsauer 2008.02217), its optimal-capacity refinement (2410.23126, NeurIPS 2024), the uniform-retrieval variant (2404.03827) and the correlated-data capacity loss (2503.09518) are all established, and ml-jku/hopfield-layers ships the metastable-state illustration. This is therefore a measurement rather than a new mechanism. Two observations were not found stated in that literature: (a) the retrieval boundary stops responding to beta above ~1 because the update degenerates to a nearest-neighbour decoder over the corrupted query (exact retrieval tracks the NN margin to within integer-overlap ties), so beta is a floor rather than a capacity dial; and (b) in the metastable regime the softmax argmax remains correct for 96.8% of queries while the retrieved state has 0.5% of a pattern's norm, i.e. the low-beta collapse is a readout failure with storage intact. The published results are theorems with retrieval-error tolerances; measured here is exact all-d-components retrieval on a joint (beta x corruption x N x d) grid with the classical Hebbian rule run on identical banks. arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this environment; web search used instead.

title: Pause/filler tokens and true recurrence buy the SAME accuracy per FLOP on serial mod-5 arithmetic chains (tie within 1-2 eval SE), both saturate after the FIRST extra application, the whole-sequence loop is 3.1-3.6x WORSE per FLOP than spending nothing, and 3 tokens of discrete intermediate supervision hit 1.000 at fewer FLOPs than 4 pause tokens
hypothesis: On left-nested modular-arithmetic chains ((a op1 b) op2 c) op3 d mod p, where difficulty is exactly the number of SEQUENTIAL reductions, extra inference compute spent as true recurrence (re-applying the same 2-layer block) buys more accuracy per FLOP than the identical FLOPs spent as k learnable pause/filler tokens (arXiv:2310.02226), and - transferring 2026-07-25_loop-test-time-compute from parity to arithmetic - training the recurrent arm with a stochastic depth schedule k~U{1..k_max} beats training it at a fixed k. Theory favours recurrence: 2505.21024 proves pause tokens buy parallel width but not serial depth, and 2404.15758 shows filler tokens only help when a parallelizable algorithm exists.
question: Which extra-inference-compute mechanism buys more accuracy per FLOP on a strictly serial task - k pause/filler tokens or k applications of a weight-tied block - when the two are put on the SAME analytic FLOP budget rather than on the same k? And does the stochastic-depth training fix that made a loop extrapolate on parity transfer to arithmetic chains?
method: One nested architecture, seven arms differing only in what occupies the gap between the expression and the answer readout. Task: left-nested chains a op1 b op2 c ... mod p=5, ops uniform from {+,-,*}, chain length n in {1,2,3} (n=3 is the backlog's ((a op1 b) op2 c) op3 d); expression right-aligned into a fixed 9-token prefix [BOS][PAD..][a op b op c][EQ] so the answer is always read at the last prefix position. Data generated fresh every step (no repeats possible); eval = 1536 held-out examples (512 per chain length) from a disjoint fixed seed; because * skews the answer marginal the reported floor is the EMPIRICAL MAJORITY-CLASS baseline 0.2715, not 1/p=0.20. Arms: (a) direct - one pass; (b) pause k - k learnable <pause> tokens appended before readout (k in {1,2,4}); (c) recur_tail k - 1 full pass then k extra applications of the same 2-layer block AT THE ANSWER POSITION ONLY against the frozen pass-1 KV cache, trained fixed AND with extra depth ~U{0..k} (k in {1,2,4}); (d) recur_full k - the same block looped k+1 times over the WHOLE sequence, fixed and stochastic (~U{1..k+1}), trained at k=2 only because it costs (k+1)x a full pass; (e) cot - discrete supervision on the 3 running intermediate values + answer, teacher-forced at train, GREEDILY DECODED at eval. The design point: recur_tail k costs the SAME FLOPs as pause k (measured relative mismatch <= 0.26%) because k pause tokens and k extra single-position block applications are both 'k extra position-applications of the 2-layer stack' - this is what makes the head-to-head a true matched-FLOP comparison instead of recurrence-gets-Nx-the-compute. FLOPs are analytic per example (QKV+proj+FFN+injection per layer-position plus 2*2*d per attended key), so matching is exact and hardware-independent; CoT is priced with a KV cache (3 emitted tokens = 3 extra positions), which places it BELOW pause k=4. Every loop iteration applies a recurrent-depth-style injection adapter z=W[h;e], so direct is exactly the recurrent model with zero extra loops - the arms are strictly nested, not different models. Held fixed everywhere: 1300 steps, batch 96, AdamW lr 2e-3 (60-step warmup), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0, 77,632 params. Secondary measurement: a test-time-k sweep (k in {1,2,4,6,8}) on the deepest recurrent arms to separate depth-robustness from compute-scaling.
architecture: 2-layer pre-LN decoder-only transformer, d_model=64, 4 heads, FFN 128, learned absolute positions, per-iteration input-injection adapter W[h;e]; 77,632 params, IDENTICAL in all seven arms

metrics.headline: at IDENTICAL analytic inference FLOPs (mismatch <=0.26%) pause tokens and tail recurrence TIE - recurrence is nominally ahead by +0.021/+0.030/+0.013 at k=1/2/4 (1.0-2.4 eval SE, one seed, and the winning variant flips from fixed to stochastic), both are worth ~+0.08 over the 0.333 direct baseline, and BOTH SATURATE AT k=1; the whole-sequence loop at 2.06x the FLOPs of pause k=4 scores 0.326 fixed / 0.279 stochastic, at or below the direct baseline and 3.1-3.6x worse per FLOP than spending nothing; stochastic depth gives no accuracy (-0.036/-0.048/+0.018) but does give depth-INVARIANCE (0.432 at test k=1 vs 0.423 at trained k=4, where fixed-k collapses to 0.262); and discrete CoT supervision on 3 intermediates reaches 1.000 at every chain length using FEWER FLOPs (1.81 MFLOP) than 4 pause tokens (1.96)

result_summary: Main hypothesis refuted by a tie, with three sharper findings underneath. (1) Put on the same analytic FLOP budget - k pause tokens vs k extra applications of the same 2-layer block at the answer position against a frozen KV cache, matched to <=0.26% - pause and recurrence are indistinguishable: recurrence leads by +0.021 (k=1), +0.030 (k=2) and +0.013 (k=4), i.e. 1.0-2.4 binomial SE on 1536 eval examples from a single seed, and the winning recurrent variant is not even consistent (fixed at k=1,2; stochastic at k=4). Both mechanisms are worth about +0.08 over the direct baseline (0.3333 -> ~0.41), which is real (~6 SE), and both SATURATE IMMEDIATELY: pause goes 0.411/0.382/0.410 and tail recurrence 0.432/0.412/0.405 as k goes 1/2/4, so nothing after the first extra position-application buys anything. (2) The literal whole-sequence loop is the worst line item in the sweep: at k=2 it costs 4.05 MFLOP (2.06x pause k=4, 3.0x direct) and scores 0.326 fixed / 0.279 stochastic - at or below the 1.35-MFLOP direct baseline, with the stochastic version indistinguishable from the 0.2715 majority-class floor; 0.081 and 0.069 accuracy per MFLOP against direct's 0.247. That independently reproduces 2026-07-25_shadow-loop-vs-depth-isoflop on a second, non-language task. (3) Stochastic depth does NOT transfer from parity as an accuracy fix (-0.036/-0.048/+0.018 vs fixed) but DOES transfer as a depth-robustness fix: over test-time k in {1,2,4,6,8} the fixed-k model only works at its trained depth (0.262/0.254/0.405/0.288/0.343) while the stochastic model works everywhere (0.432/0.437/0.423/0.408/0.390) - and is already at its best score at k=1, so it has learned a depth-invariant fixed point whose extra iterations are free of charge AND free of benefit. Invariance, not compute-scaling. (4) The reference upper line is brutal and is the practically useful number: discrete supervision on the three running intermediate values reaches 1.000 accuracy at EVERY chain length (greedily decoded, not teacher-forced) at 1.81 MFLOP - FEWER FLOPs than 4 pause tokens (1.96) - for 0.553 accuracy per MFLOP, 1.9x the best latent mechanism and +0.57 over the best latent arm / +0.67 over direct. CoT converts one n-step serial problem into n independent 1-step problems and a 2-layer transformer solves a single mod-5 op perfectly; neither pause tokens nor latent recurrence discovers that decomposition. Consistent with the theory (2505.21024: pause tokens add parallel width, not serial depth; 2404.15758: filler tokens need a parallelizable algorithm) and with our own coconut-toy-graph (pause 0.687 vs discrete CoT 0.937). Every latent arm also degrades with chain length (pause k=4: 0.529/0.381/0.320 at n=1/2/3) and sits within 0.05-0.09 of the majority baseline at n=3, i.e. the extra compute buys EASY instances, not deep ones - the opposite of a working serial-compute mechanism. Caveats stated in the README: one seed (only the large effects survive plausible seed variance), and an undertrained iso-compute regime (1300 steps; a pilot shows the task still improving past 2000 steps), so these are learning-speed-at-fixed-budget rankings rather than converged-accuracy rankings.

title: Removing the hidden-state dependence of the gates (minGRU/minLSTM) costs 0.36-0.64 exact match vs a standard GRU on selective copy at matched params and steps - and the cost is ORDERING older items (hard recency profile: last 2 slots perfect, rest near chance), not remembering distant ones; depth (2 layers: 0.39->0.82) and 3x steps (0.39->0.96) substitute for the missing gate at k=4
hypothesis: arXiv:2410.01201 strips the hidden-state dependence out of the GRU/LSTM gates - exactly what makes the recurrence a parallel scan - and claims minGRU/minLSTM match full RNNs broadly; the Mamba literature (arXiv:2312.00752) claims selective copy is the task that needs content-dependent state updates. For minGRU these CONFLICT: its gate sees the current input (so it can decide 'this token is data, write it') but never the state (so it cannot decide 'this is the 3rd data token, put it in slot 3'). We predicted minGRU loses to a standard GRU at matched params/steps on selective copy, with the gap widening in k (tokens to memorise) rather than in L (sequence length).
question: Does removing the hidden-state dependence of the gates cost anything on a task that needs content-dependent gating, and if so is the loss in memory span or in ordering/slot assignment - and can depth or extra training budget buy it back?
method: Hand-rolled PyTorch cells behind a byte-identical wrapper: embedding(48) -> n_layers x (cell + LayerNorm) -> GELU bottleneck(64) -> k linear slot heads on the FINAL hidden state (no autoregressive decode phase, so the comparison is purely about the recurrence). Cells: standard GRU (nn.GRU; r, z and candidate see x AND h), minGRU exactly as in the paper (h_t=(1-z_t)h_{t-1}+z_t h~_t, z_t=sigmoid(Linear(x_t)), h~_t=Linear(x_t)) run in the sequential form (identical maths to the parallel scan), and minLSTM (f,i=sigmoid(Linear(x)), normalised f'=f/(f+i), i'=i/(f+i)). Task: Mamba-style selective copy - length-L sequence of a single blank token with k data tokens (vocab 8) at uniformly random positions; target = the k data values IN ORDER OF APPEARANCE. Sweep L in {32,64} x k in {4,8}. Every arm's hidden width is fitted so TOTAL params ~= 60k (59.2k-60.3k actual); because minGRU has no hidden->hidden matrices this gives it a 3.3x LARGER state than the GRU (d=350 vs 106), making the test conservative against the hypothesis. Held fixed: 600 steps, batch 32, AdamW lr 3e-3 (OneCycle 10% warmup), wd 0.01, grad-clip 1.0; fresh data every step; eval 1024 fixed held-out sequences per cell from a disjoint seed (binomial SE ~0.016). Controls/probes: minGRU at the GRU's STATE SIZE (d=106, 20k params) as a capacity control; minGRU at 3x the step budget (separates 'learns slowly' from 'cannot'); 1-vs-2-layer GRU and minGRU on the easiest and hardest cells (does depth recover state-dependent gating?). Diagnostics: per-output-slot accuracy, and the mean learned input gate z on noise vs data tokens. 24 training runs, 606s wall clock, single CPU thread.
architecture: 1-layer (and 2-layer probe) recurrent models at ~60k total params each: standard GRU d=104-106, minGRU d=338-350, minLSTM d=260-270, plus a shared embedding/LayerNorm/bottleneck/slot-head readout identical across arms

metrics.headline: at matched TOTAL params (~60k) and matched steps (600) on selective copy, a 1-layer standard GRU beats a 1-layer minGRU by +0.611/+0.644 exact match at k=4 (1.000 vs 0.389/0.356) and by +0.381/+0.357 at k=8 (0.382/0.357 vs 0.001/0.000), unchanged by doubling L from 32 to 64 - the deficit tracks the NUMBER OF ITEMS, not the span; minGRU demonstrably learned the input-only half of selectivity (mean gate z 0.13-0.25 on noise vs 0.40-0.44 on data) and fails only on ordering, showing a hard recency profile (per-slot accuracy [0.31,0.34,0.35,0.39,0.38,0.41,0.90,1.00] at k=8 vs the GRU's uniformly high [0.94,...,1.00]); it is not capacity (minGRU has 3.3x the GRU's state at matched params and a state-size-matched minGRU loses only 0.11 more) and not a minGRU quirk (minLSTM is identical); but 3x steps takes minGRU from 0.389 to 0.964 at k=4 and 2 layers take it from 0.389 to 0.821, so the deficit is a large constant factor of depth/training compute rather than a proven representational wall

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed, with the mechanism localised and two honest qualifiers. (1) At ~60k matched TOTAL params and 600 matched steps, a 1-layer GRU beats a 1-layer minGRU on every difficulty cell of selective copy: exact match 1.000 vs 0.389 (L=32,k=4), 1.000 vs 0.356 (L=64,k=4), 0.382 vs 0.001 (L=32,k=8), 0.357 vs 0.000 (L=64,k=8); gaps of +0.36 to +0.64 against a 0.016 eval SE, and the same picture on a second seed. This is despite the comparison being conservative: matched params give minGRU a 3.3x LARGER hidden state (d=350 vs 106) because it has no hidden->hidden matrices. (2) The deficit tracks k, not L. Doubling the sequence length 32->64 changes nothing (minGRU 0.389->0.356, GRU 1.000->1.000); doubling k 4->8 collapses minGRU (0.389->0.001). So the missing hidden-state gate does not cost memory SPAN, it costs the ability to keep k items distinguishable and ordered. (3) minGRU learned the half of selectivity a gate can implement from the current token alone: its mean input gate is 0.13-0.25 on blank tokens and 0.40-0.44 on data tokens - correct 'hold on noise, write on data' behaviour. What it cannot do is condition the write on what is already stored. (4) The signature of that failure is a hard recency profile in per-slot accuracy: at L=64,k=8 minGRU scores [0.31,0.34,0.35,0.39,0.38,0.41,0.90,1.00] over slots 1->8 - the last two data tokens perfectly, everything older barely above the 0.125 chance floor - while the GRU is uniformly high and U-shaped [0.94,0.72,0.78,0.83,0.89,0.93,0.97,1.00]. An input-only gate can only run a leaky integrator over the tokens it decides to write, so order survives only as MAGNITUDE and older items fall below readout resolution after 2-3 writes; the GRU can use its state as an addressable buffer. (5) Not capacity: the state-size-matched minGRU (20k params, d=106) loses only a further 0.11 at k=4 and nothing at k=8, an order of magnitude less than the GRU gap. Not a minGRU quirk: minLSTM is statistically identical (0.424/0.406 at k=4, 0.000 at k=8) - it is the input-only-gate family. QUALIFIERS: (a) at k=4 the gap is mostly LEARNING SPEED - 3x the steps takes minGRU from 0.389 to 0.964, so the input-only gate can represent a 4-item ordered buffer, it just needs several times the optimisation budget; at k=8 3x steps moves per-token 0.510->0.673 but exact match only 0.000->0.003, so the deficit there is at least much larger than 3x and we did not reach the closing point. (b) DEPTH SUBSTITUTES FOR THE MISSING GATE: a 2-layer minGRU at the same params jumps 0.389->0.821 at L=32,k=4, exactly as expected since layer 2's gates see layer 1's output, which is a function of layer 1's accumulated state - this plausibly explains why the paper's own 3-layer minGRU reaches 99.5% on its selective-copy benchmark while our 1-layer version does not. The honest statement is therefore not 'minGRU cannot do selective copy' but 'removing the hidden-state gate costs a large constant factor of depth and training compute on exactly the task that needs content-dependent state updates, and the price is paid in ordering older items rather than in remembering distant ones'. Caveats in the README: 1-layer main sweep, 600 steps, 60k params, vocab 8 (paper uses 16), 2 seeds on the headline pair and 1 elsewhere; these are learning-speed-at-fixed-budget rankings.

So the head-to-head that its central claim implies has, to our search, never been run on selective copy. Prior art therefore covers the minGRU-on-selective-copy number itself (hence partial-prior-art, not novel), but not the ablation. arXiv/OpenAlex APIs 403 from this environment; WebSearch plus a direct read of the paper PDF used instead.

title: Induction heads form as a phase transition and weight-space K-composition LEADS it by 601 steps (133 steps under a strictly online criterion) where the attention-pattern scores LAG - but the rise is shared by all 16 head pairs, overshoots 1.68x and decays, and fires a late false positive on a model where induction is impossible
hypothesis: In a 2-layer attention-only transformer (no MLPs, no LayerNorm) trained on periodically-repeating random-token sequences, the in-context loss (loss on repeated tokens minus loss on first-occurrence tokens) drops as a sharp phase transition, and the K-composition strength ||W_QK^(1) W_OV^(0)||_F of the winning (previous-token head, induction head) pair starts rising BEFORE the drop - a genuinely leading progress measure, unlike the spectral-entropy measures that LAGGED the jump in 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition.
question: Does a weight-only composition measure LEAD the induction-head phase transition, and how does it rank head-to-head against the standard activation-space diagnostics (previous-token score, induction/prefix-matching score) measured on the same runs - under an artifact-prone fraction-of-movement criterion, an earliest-detection variant, and a strictly online absolute threshold?
method: 2-layer attention-only transformer, 4 heads per layer, trained on periodic random-token sequences: per sample a period p ~ U{12..24} is drawn, the first p tokens are sampled WITHOUT replacement from a 128-symbol vocab (so the induction target is unambiguous and the diagnostics are exact), and the sequence is tiled to length 48. The per-sample random period blocks the purely positional 'attend to i-p' shortcut that the classic fixed 'second half repeats the first half' construction leaves open. Target index j <= p-1 is a first occurrence (irreducible, floor = log 128 = 4.852 nats); j >= p+1 is solvable ONLY through an induction circuit; j = p is excluded from both masks because the query token at p-1 has no earlier occurrence to induct from. Four measures logged every 20 steps (plus every 5 steps up to step 100, so an early onset is resolvable) on a FIXED 192-sequence held-out eval batch: (1) in-context loss delta = mean loss(repeat) - mean loss(first occurrence); (2) previous-token score = layer-0 head attention mass at position i-1; (3) induction score = layer-1 head attention mass at (previous occurrence of the current token) + 1; (4) composition scores for all 4x4 head pairs, ||A W_OV^(0)||_F / (||A||_F ||W_OV^(0)||_F) with A = W_QK^(1) (K-composition), W_QK^(1)T (Q) and W_OV^(1) (V), each against a SPECTRUM-PRESERVING NULL of 16 random orthogonal rotations R applied as A(R W_OV) - which destroys alignment while leaving both singular-value spectra intact, converting a raw composition number into a z-score. Onsets are computed under three criteria so nothing rests on one: (A) 50% of total init->final movement, matched to the grokking experiment and requiring the final model; (B) 10% of movement, the earliest-detection variant of the same family; (C) ONLINE absolute thresholds using no future information - composition z > 5 vs its rotation null, attention scores > 2x their uniform-attention baseline (0.0736 prev / 0.0331 induction), loss delta < -5% of log V (-0.243 nats), all sustained 2 consecutive evals. Plus the truncation control that demolished the spectral result in the grokking run: criterion A recomputed as if training had STOPPED at the transition. Held fixed: 1800 steps, batch 64, AdamW lr 3e-3 (100-step warmup), wd 0.01, betas (0.9, 0.98), 3 seeds. Two controls: (a) a false-positive control - an identical model trained on i.i.d. NON-repeating tokens, where an induction head is impossible, evaluated on the same repeating eval batch; (b) Q- and V-composition of the same head pair against their own nulls, as a specificity check on which side of the layer-1 head reads the layer-0 head.
architecture: 2-layer attention-only transformer, NO MLPs and NO LayerNorm (so the W_QK^(1) @ W_OV^(0) path is exact with no normalization to fold through), d_model 64, 4 heads per layer (head dim 16), learned absolute positions, untied unembed; 52,224 params

task: in-context copying of repeated random tokens; solvable only by a previous-token head in layer 0 K-composing with an induction head in layer 1
compute: CPU single-threaded (torch.set_num_threads(1), OMP_NUM_THREADS=1), 368.2s wall clock for all 4 training runs + per-eval diagnostics + chart, against a ~720s box

metrics.headline: in-context loss delta +0.00 -> -5.00 nats, phase transition at step 707.6 (10-90% width 439.7 steps = 24% of training); K-composition of the winning pair leads by 601.0 steps under the 50%-of-movement criterion and 133.3 steps under the online absolute-threshold criterion; prev-token score -166.5 / -360.0, induction score -64.8 / -220.0 (positive = leads)

result_summary: Hypothesis confirmed on TIMING, refuted on SPECIFICITY. (1) The phase transition reproduces cleanly at 52,224 params in 90 seconds of CPU: the in-context loss delta (loss on repeat tokens minus loss on first-occurrence tokens) goes 0.00 -> -5.00 nats, with loss on repeat tokens falling 4.85 -> 0.087 while first-occurrence loss RISES to 5.08 (above the log-128 = 4.852 floor) as capacity is spent on copying; final prev-token score 0.37-0.44 (5.0-5.9x the 0.0736 uniform baseline) and induction score 0.585-0.620 (17.7-18.7x the 0.0331 baseline). The transition sits at step 707.6 (728/689/706 per seed) after ~500 flat steps, but is honestly a fast sigmoid rather than a discontinuity: 10-90% width 440 steps = 24% of training (648/366/305), and seed 0 is two-stage (a shelf at -4.2 from step ~850 to ~1250, then a second drop). (2) K-composition LEADS under all three criteria and the two activation-space diagnostics LAG under all three, with all 3 seeds agreeing in sign everywhere: winning-pair K-composition +601.0 steps (609/592/601) on the 50%-of-movement criterion, +458.0 on the 10% variant, and +133.3 (40/140/220) on the strictly online absolute threshold; best-of-16-pairs +594.6 / +445.2 / +206.7; previous-token score -166.5 / -45.8 / -360.0; induction score -64.8 / -55.2 / -220.0. In online step numbers: composition crosses at step 120-280, the loss at 320-340, the induction score at 480-600, the previous-token score at 660-720. At the moment of the loss transition composition has already completed 168% of its total movement (it overshoots) while the attention scores have completed only 30% and 34% of theirs. (3) The lead is NOT a truncation artifact, and the artifact that ruined the grokking result is directly visible on the other measures: recomputing the 50%-of-movement criterion on data truncated at the transition moves composition only +601 -> +521, but flips previous-token -166 -> +24 and induction -65 -> +1.5. So the same manoeuvre that manufactured fake spectral leads in 2026-07-25_grokking-modular-addition manufactures fake leads here too - for the attention measures, not for composition. (4) The elevation is specific to the KEY side, exactly as the Anthropic framework predicts: for the same head pair at the end of training, K-composition sits at z = +6.09 above its spectrum-preserving rotation null while Q-composition is at z = -6.47 and V-composition at z = -7.45 (raw 0.184 vs 0.052 vs 0.048) - the layer-1 head reads the layer-0 head on the key side and actively avoids it on the query and value sides, recovered from weights alone. (5) But the measure is a coarse alarm, not a circuit identifier, and this is where the hypothesis breaks. The early rise is BROAD: at the transition the winning pair exceeds the mean of the other 15 pairs by only +0.043 raw (per seed +0.110 / -0.007 / +0.025), i.e. all 16 pairs rise together and only separate afterwards. The pair identified by the final attention patterns is the top-composition pair in just 1 of 3 seeds (winning-pair final z 13.44 / 0.10 / 4.74 vs best-of-16 z 13.44 / 11.37 / 7.99); in seed 1 that pair's composition has returned to the null by the end of training even though it crossed z > 5 at step 180, so the weight alignment is a TRANSIENT SCAFFOLD (the 1.68 overshoot) rather than a persistent signature, and the final score is a poor fingerprint even when the trajectory was a good predictor. And the i.i.d. false-positive control, where an induction head is impossible, behaves correctly on everything activation-based - delta stays at +0.0001 nats, prev-token 0.0725 and induction 0.0330 are exactly the uniform-attention baselines, none of their online onsets ever fire - yet its best-of-16 composition still reaches z = 4.48 and crosses the z > 5 threshold at step 1720. That is a real false positive; it is 14x later than the trained models' step-120 onset and it brackets seed 2's own winning-pair z of 4.74. Net: composition strength LEADS where spectral entropy LAGGED, and survives the control that killed the spectral result - a genuine positive for weight-space progress measures - but what it announces is 'a circuit is assembling', not 'this circuit is assembling', and it can announce it on a model that has no circuit to assemble. Caveats: 3 seeds, one task, one architecture, one hyperparameter setting, a synthetic task engineered so the transition is findable, and the winning pair is selected from the final model (the max-over-pairs variant, which is causally online, behaves the same).

novelty_check.conclusion: Every ingredient is published separately but the head-to-head is not. Olsson et al. 2022 supply the setting and composition scores as a diagnostic; read directly, they describe the phase change as abrupt, explicitly report NO leading indicator ('there is not some known exogenous factor precipitating everything'), and show composition scores rising DURING the window - with only 15 snapshots for their large models, i.e. too little time resolution to see a lead if one existed. The 2021 Mathematical Framework supplies the K/Q/V-composition definitions. arXiv:2511.16893 predicts the formation STEP from a batch-x-context scaling law (U_PT = T*sqrt(BC), r=0.98) on a 2-layer toy GPT-2 over 1B tokens using the prefix-matching score - a data-statistics predictor, not a model-internal one, and with no leading-indicator comparison. arXiv:2404.07129 clamps three subcircuits causally during training and finds they co-evolve, without ranking measures by lead time. arXiv:2509.22947 shows attention-map induction signatures are not load-bearing, using random-head ablation rather than weight-space composition. To our search, no prior work puts a weight-only K-composition score head-to-head against the attention-pattern scores as competing LEADING progress measures on the same runs, with (a) a spectrum-preserving random-orthogonal-rotation null that turns composition into a z-score, (b) an online absolute threshold alongside the artifact-prone fraction-of-movement criterion AND the truncation control that separates them, (c) an i.i.d. false-positive control where induction is impossible, and (d) Q- and V-composition of the same pair as specificity controls. arXiv and OpenAlex return HTTP 403 from this environment (known; scripts/novelty_check.py returned 'unchecked'), so the verdict rests on web search plus direct reads of the four sources above.
